title: Mistä: answering with -lta and -ltä
focus: Mistä also asks where from with the at/on family. Mistä sinä tulet? — Tulen asemalta.

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Where are you coming from?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. The elative is the from-inside form, answering where from. Mistä also asks where from with the at/on family. Change the taught location's -lla/-llä to -lta/-ltä: asemalla (“at the station”) becomes asemalta (“from the station”). The complete question means “Where are you coming from”.

sentenceExplanation.translation: Where are you coming from?
sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking where from + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)
